::: {#thm-bh-fdr}
#### The BH procedure controls the FDR under independence

Suppose the $m$ p-values are independent and each true null hypothesis has a p-value that is uniform on $[0, 1]$.
Then the [BH procedure](#def-bh) at level $q$ satisfies

$$\text{FDR} = \frac{m_0}{m} q \le q.$$

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
#### Source

Benjamini and Hochberg [-@benjamini1995controlling],
which proves the result for any configuration of false null hypotheses.
The proof is omitted here.
:::

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

::: {#exm-bh-fdr}
#### FDR of the BH procedure in the simulated family

In the simulated family of @exm-rejection-counts the p-values are independent and $m_0 / m = 0.9$,
so @thm-bh-fdr gives $\text{FDR} = 0.9 \times 0.05 =$ `r 0.9 * 0.05` at $q = 0.05$.
Repeating the simulation 2000 times with BH:

```{r}
#| label: fdr-bh
#| code-fold: false
set.seed(576)
sim_counts$bh <- run_simulation(function(p) bh_reject(p, 0.05))
summarize_counts(sim_counts$bh)
```

The estimated FDR, `r round(summarize_counts(sim_counts$bh)[["FDR"]], 3)`,
is close to the theoretical value `r 0.9 * 0.05`.
BH also finds `r round(100 * summarize_counts(sim_counts$bh)[["power"]])`% of the false null hypotheses,
more than Holm's procedure,
and in exchange it makes at least one false positive in
`r round(100 * summarize_counts(sim_counts$bh)[["FWER"]])`% of the repetitions.
:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

::: {#rem-bh-dependence}
#### BH under dependence

Gene expression levels are usually correlated,
and @thm-bh-fdr assumes independence.
@benjamini2001control proved that BH still controls the FDR at level $q$ under a form of positive dependence among the p-values,
and that the procedure run at level $q / \sum_{k=1}^m (1/k)$ controls it under any dependence.
@james2021islr2e [ch. 13] and @efron2016computer [ch. 15] discuss the procedure in practice.
:::
